messages.content: "Can you help me create a piece of music in D Minor with a tempo of 120 beats per minute and then generate an audio signal with a frequency of 440 Hz and an amplitude of 0.5? After that, I would like to generate another piece of music in E Major with a tempo of 90 beats per minute and a time signature of 3/4. Finally, generate another audio signal with a frequency of 300 Hz, an amplitude of 0.7, and a duration of 5 seconds."

function.name: audio_generate
function.description: Generate an audio signal given a frequency, amplitude, and duration. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

frequency.description: Frequency of the audio signal in Hz.

amplitude.description: Amplitude of the audio signal. This is a float type value.

duration.description: Duration of the audio signal in seconds. Default is 1 second if not specified. This is a float type value.

function.name: music_generate
function.description: Generate a piece of music given a key, tempo, and time signature. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

key.description: The key of the piece, e.g., C Major.

tempo.description: Tempo of the piece in beats per minute.

time_signature.description: Time signature of the piece, e.g., 4/4. Default is '4/4' if not specified.

message.reasoning:
The user wants us to do two things: generate music pieces (with key, tempo, time signature) and generate audio signals (frequency, amplitude, duration). They want us to call the functions accordingly.

We have two functions: audio_generate and music_generate. We need to call them in order:

1. Generate a piece of music in D Minor with tempo 120 bpm. No time signature specified, so default 4/4. So we call music_generate with key="D Minor", tempo=120.

2. Then generate an audio signal with frequency 440 Hz, amplitude 0.5. No duration specified, so default 1 second. So call audio_generate with frequency=440, amplitude=0.5.

3. Then generate another piece of music in E Major with tempo 90 bpm and time signature 3/4. So call music_generate with key="E Major", tempo=90, time_signature="3/4".

4. Finally generate another audio signal with frequency 300 Hz, amplitude 0.7, duration 5 seconds. So call audio_generate with frequency=300, amplitude=0.7, duration=5.

We can either combine them into one call or separate calls. The guidelines say we can make multiple calls. But we might want to do them sequentially. The best approach is to call each function separately. The user didn't specify that they want the results printed out. They just said "help me create ...". So we will call the functions accordingly.
